transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Julia Park (Transcend Head of ML), Evan Brooks (CTO), Rita Gomez (SRE)

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we, um, this is Sofia from Redwood, and Marcus our solutions engineer is with me. you all good on audio?
[00:10] Julia: Yes, thanks. We can hear you. Thanks for doing this.
[00:13] Marcus: Great. quick agenda: understand your current infra, workloads, why you're considering Dedicated, isolation and compliance needs, and then sizing/burst strategy. we'll wrap with next steps.
[00:25] Evan: Perfect. high level, we're building a customer-facing assistant on top of our financial docs and transaction logs. latency is a big deal — we want p95 < 150ms for short queries. cost is also sensitive, so we want to understand reserved capacity pricing vs hosted.
[00:40] Julia: And security — data residency, KMS, SOC2 — we can't have customer PII leaving our VPC.
[00:48] Marcus: Understood. can I ask a few quick qualifiers around throughput and model types?
[00:52] Evan: Sure. baseline is around 30 qps during business hours, peaking to about 150 qps during marketing pushes. average request size is short prompts, ~40–80 tokens, some longer doc retrieval workflows. Models: we're experimenting with a fine-tuned 13B for responses and gpt-style embeddings for search.
[01:13] Marcus: Ok that helps. So Dedicated typically maps well when you need guaranteed GPUs and isolation — reserved pools with predictable throughput. You mentioned bursts to 150 qps, we usually recommend a base reserved pool sized for normal load + burst capacity (either pre-purchased burst or autoscale to a higher tier) — have you thought about how important hard guarantees are during those spikes vs acceptable throttling?
[01:34] Julia: During marketing spikes we need the experience to be snappy. we can tolerate brief queueing for non-critical flows but core assistant must stay under the SLA.
[01:42] Rita: Also ops question: we run in AWS us-east-1 and need VPC peering or PrivateLink options; can Redwood Dedicated be deployed in our VPC/on‑prem?
[01:51] Marcus: Yes. Redwood Private provides VPC and on‑prem options; Dedicated can be deployed in a customer VPC depending on the package — often folks start with Dedicated hosted by Redwood and then move to Private if they need full control. we'll share specifics; there are two deployment patterns: managed Private control plane with customer VPC, or fully on‑prem for air‑gapped.
[02:10] Evan: And how about KMS and audit logs? We need CMKs and full request audit logging to our SIEM.
[02:16] Marcus: We support KMS integrations and can forward logs. I'll get you the SOC2 artifacts and our audit logging docs. small note — in some older notes our product name shows as "Reedwood" in transcriptions, ignore that — ha.
[02:29] Julia: (laughs) noted.
[02:31] Sofia: On cost, do you have a target monthly committed spend or contract length in mind?
[02:36] Evan: We'd prefer a predictable monthly commit. probably looking at a 6–12 month pilot and then annual reserved if it works. budget is TBD but want to model 3 scenarios: baseline 30 qps steady, medium = 60 qps, burst = 150 qps.
[02:50] Marcus: Makes sense. For reserved pools we size GPUs by expected sustained concurrency and model latency footprint. e.g., a 13B quantized to 4-bit on A100-like nodes gives X requests/sec per GPU for 40–80 token sequences. we'll run targeted benchmarks to map your exact workload.
[03:10] Rita: How tolerant are you of quantization artifacts? We need consistent quality for some regulated responses.
[03:16] Julia: For a lot of the assistant flows quality must be near current fine-tuned baseline; we can tolerate minimal regression but want a way to A/B test.
[03:23] Marcus: Agreed — Redwood Optimize includes quantization profiles and quality monitoring. for Dedicated pilots we usually recommend a canary model variant running on the same pool to validate no regressions, and automated fallback to a higher-precision variant if quality drops.
[03:38] Evan: Nice. canredwood route to hosted fallback if our Dedicated pool is saturated?
[03:43] Marcus: Yes, there's smart routing and fallback policies — route by latency or cost and failover to compatible variants in Hosted or lower priority Dedicated tiers. note that data residency and PII policies might change route options — you would control those policies.
[03:59] Julia: About burst strategy: you mentioned pre-purchased burst and autoscale. what are the typical limits and warm-up times?
[04:07] Marcus: Warm-up is mostly about loading KV cache and model weights; we keep cold-starts low by keeping hot-models resident if you expect frequent bursts. autoscale can spin additional instances but there can be a few seconds to tens of seconds for spin-up depending on size. pre-bought burst capacity is the way to get hard guarantees for short spikes — that's reserved but billed differently.
[04:26] Evan: So for marketing pushes that last 5–15 minutes, pre-bought burst seems safer.
[04:31] Sofia: Exactly, and we can model the cost tradeoff. we'll provide a 6-month cost model for the three traffic scenarios.
[04:38] Rita: Security detail: do you support bringing your own HSM / customer-managed keys?
[04:43] Marcus: Yep, BYOK is supported via KMS/HSM integrations. we'll include integration notes. Also we can ship audit logs to your S3 or SIEM with TTL controls.
[04:55] Julia: Good. one more — backups of models and weights, who manages that for Dedicated?
[05:00] Marcus: For Redwood-managed Dedicated, we handle model artifacts in a private storage tier but you can also bring and manage your weights in your own object store for Private deployments. backups are part of the Dedicated support plan if you need snapshot retention.
[05:12] Evan: Can you run a quick example calculation? say 30 qps baseline, 40 tokens avg, what's the rough GPU need and monthly cost ballpark?
[05:21] Marcus: I don't want to misquote numbers without the benchmark but roughly, a single A100-class GPU can handle N requests/sec for a 13B at those token lengths with quantization. I'll put concrete numbers in the pricing sheet — we typically show per-GPU throughput, unit cost per 1M tokens, and committed discounts.
[05:38] Sofia: We'll include a modeled SKU mapping: base GPUs for steady state, a burst SKU, and optional Private add-on.
[05:45] Julia: For the pilot, we'd want a minimal Dedicated pool that matches our baseline and a plan to test burst via a scheduled load test.
[05:53] Marcus: Perfect — benchmarks we run are: representative payloads, KV/prefix cache warm vs cold, embedding throughput, and latency percentiles. we'll also capture memory/KV usage to inform autoscale policies.
[06:08] Rita: On networking — we need PrivateLink. any constraints on egress IPs or firewall rules?
[06:14] Marcus: We'll share the network diagram. typically Dedicated in a customer VPC uses your subnets and NAT/Egress is controlled by you. For Hosted Dedicated, egress IPs are documented and we can reserve ranges.
[06:25] Evan: Who will be the day‑to‑day contacts post-contract?
[06:28] Sofia: You'll have an AE and a named SE for onboarding, plus optional SRE support. SLA levels determine priority and response times.
[06:36] Julia: Regarding SLAs, do you attach latency SLOs in the contract or just uptime?
[06:40] Marcus: Primarily uptime SLAs, but we offer latency targets for Dedicated agreements and will include latency-based alerts and tracing. we'll need to agree on traffic profile to make them contractual.
[06:52] Evan: What about model updates and version pinning? we want deterministic behavior during audits.
[06:57] Marcus: You can pin model versions per-route and do canary rollouts. Redwood's deployment abstraction lets you fix a version and only update after validation. Logs and eval hooks let you trace regressions back to versions.
[07:09] Julia: Perfect. any known limitations with private deployments around hardware choices? like we prefer certain GPU vendors.
[07:15] Marcus: For Private/on‑prem we support common datacenter GPUs; for managed Dedicated we have A100-like nodes. if you need a specific GPU type, that's doable for Private but may affect lead time and pricing.
[07:27] Evan: Ok that's good to know.
[07:29] Sofia: Quick recap — action items and next steps: we will send pricing and SKU mapping, Marcus will share the benchmark plan, Transcend will share security contact and SOC2 scope, and we'll tentatively schedule a Private/VPC demo mid‑March.
[07:43] Julia: Sounds good. thanks everyone.
[07:45] Rita: Thanks.
[07:46] Evan: Appreciate it.
[07:48] Sofia: One last thing, competitors — you mentioned exploring Anthropic and OpenAI — anything specific that pushed you toward Dedicated?
[07:55] Julia: Mainly isolation and cost predictability. Hosted APIs are simpler but margins at our scale and compliance needs push us toward Dedicated/Private.
[08:05] Marcus: Cool. We'll include benchmark comparisons and a note on when Dedicated makes sense vs continuing with hosted.
[08:12] Sofia: Alright we'll follow up with the materials. thanks everyone, bye.
